content.text:
Yeah, I think Nicole said it well, but Spencer, pleasure to meet you. I'm the DPS over here on the Mulesoft side of the business. Been here for the last seven and a half years, and I lead our small business unit for North America.
So here to learn more. Serve as your exact sponsor if you brought on Mulesoft and see how we can help make you more successful. Nice to meet you.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: Nice to meet you. Thanks for jumping on.

All right, so looking at our agenda for today, we'll just start off with a quick read-back to make sure we're aligned on everything from the previous conversations. From there, we'll dive right into the proposal, and we'll save some time at the end for Q&A, and we'll wrap up with next steps.
So if that works for you all, I will jump right. So setting the baseline here, when we look at your current operation, Airfleet is handling around 1,000 loan applications a year, and the volume nearly doubles during peak season, which starts in November.
Right now, every single application relies on a heavy manual intake process. So packages are consolidated by hand, which takes around 45 minutes per package. Then data is being rekeyed twice, first into Excel and then into Salesforce. This turns a single package into up to a full day of just preparation and scaling from here means burning out the current team, bringing on temporary staff, or just continuing to absorb all of that manual work.
Our goal with Mulesoft is to automate that entire flow. So from box extraction to Salesforce in the Excel worksheet. So a package that takes up to a full day to prepare today will be analysis-ready in just 3 minutes.
So your team's going to get that time back to spend on actual risk analysis and decision-making instead of data entry. And that's going to dramatically increase your speed to market. When we look at what this actually means for the business, it comes down to really three major outcomes, first being driving efficiency. When we're taking a total package processing from an entire day to just 3 minutes.
Then on top of that, we're giving your underwriters back over 750 hours of manual work every single year. And consolidation alone. So we're going to allow your team to focus on high-value work instead of just that tedious data entry. Secondly, scalable growth. You get a scalable solution that automates growing loan volume without having to add additional headcount or rely on offshoring resources.
Third, keeping your data secure while leveraging AI. I know this was a really important topic for Jim and the team. So being able to automate this while keeping all the sensitive financial data strictly inside your existing environment is really crucial.
We want to be crystal clear that everything is going to stay inside of Salesforce and Box the entire time. So nothing ever routes through a third-party AI model, Mulesoft, or store copy of your files, and nothing is ever going to be exposed externally.
I know that was a really important piece into this evaluation. Anything you would add there?

content.text: No, Nicole. We have more... We'll dig in a little bit more in detail here. So nothing that I would add here. That did a nice job, but I would say... Spencer falls on this... There is this bang on... Is there something we're missing or anything you guys would have?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
No, I think that you know, then that's great because you know, obviously we were looking for efficiency and then obviously security is a huge issue because of all the sensitive information that we're dealing with and the fact that, you know, we don't have to we would it'll grow with us either as we grow. All very important.
So I don't know if. If you have anything to add.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: No, I agree with Ann.

content.speaker: Speaker 5
content.text:
There, right on. Awesome. So I'm going to take this one. So this is really talking about everything Nicole just mentioned, but more how we actually make that happen. This is not new for you guys. We have been basically talking about this the entire time, but we want to just read this back to you and make sure we understand the problem statement exactly how you're solving for it.
So we're really looking at the current state. Starting from the top there and moving over left to right, we have loan applications coming in, including the multiple types of documents we've already talked about. These are received via the box upload portal. There is an issue here, which is to say staff is manually doing some of this stuff, so we're going to rename everything to handle the logistics of all the packages. Nothing is really automated in this process, but once we're in Excel, we're going to manually punch that data in as well.
Then at the end of that, there's even a third part of this where we are doing this a third time, keying this data back into Salesforce. This takes a long time to knock out. There are now multiple pathways for potential errors with duplicate entry, etc., but it's just very time-consuming and not scalable, which is why...
You guys are the proposal on your desk. So, let's offer this to somebody else. Do we understand this problem generally, right? I know we've been talking about it a bunch, but do we feel good about this?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Yeah, I do.

content.speaker: Speaker 5
content.text:
Okay, right on. Then restating again here with Mulesoft, we're going to be launching that box portal. So when something new comes in, we are instantly going to take it. We are going to identify what kind of document that is. We are going to rename it accordingly, store it accordingly, and then from there we're going to extract the data as well. Throw it into the underwriting worksheet and Excel so that you can have the calculations ready to go there, and then from there your team can just move on. Instead of doing document entry and extraction, they are doing underwriting and decision-making.
That is going to be the happy place that is the end state that we are all shooting for here. Kailash, it seems, is going to play a big role here in working with you guys to make sure that vision looks exactly like you wanted it to.
If there's nothing else, we'll move on. And, Spencer, do we feel like this is the solution that we're looking for right now?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Yes, I do.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: I just have one question. Just a confirmation to make sure that we all have the right scope here. Is there anything that lives on the Excel sheet calculation, a field that gets entered into Salesforce that we would want to pull off that sheet and enter into Salesforce?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
Yes. So there's actually a separate spreadsheet in that Excel workbook that captures the data that we put into... I think it's called the credit and analysis section of the Opportunity. Yes, that's what it's called.
So I mean, the data could actually just... I think that would be a good place to map it from there.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: But there's going to be a set of data that comes from the documents and then a set of data that comes from the Excel sheet, and those... That data is going to finalize itself in Salesforce.

content.speaker: Speaker 5
content.text: Correct. Right on. Does that track with what you're thinking?

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text:
Yeah. As I mentioned earlier in our call, I wanted to make sure that whatever is being done today in Excel, we will have the same data in Salesforce, and we will have the data parallelly inserted into Salesforce. The Excel to make sure that whatever calculations that you are seeing in Excel will reflect the same in Salesforce.
Once you are confident, we will have a toggle switch that you can toggle off to stop getting into Excel and just push it into Salesforce.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: Thank you.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: No...

It's an annual total of $3,535. This is recurring. This gives you the ability to process 300,000 pages of documents yearly, as we had talked about a little bit there. A lot of this stuff is... Whether it's five pages or 100, we really just need to scan the first couple to know what it is and get the information we need out of it.
That's the only portion that will be there. The rest is there to be utilized for other use cases, future use cases, etc. You have the backbone of your soft, which is the Anypoint platform, to allow you to make those integrations that once I've extracted the data, I'm able to push that data into Excel, into Salesforce back and forth, and of course, tapping into Box to get the data in the first place. The terms here we have a quarterly billing. We know that you guys are on a tight timeline. We have a busy season. November and December, we have to be ready to go by then.
So we have this right now with a contract execution for the end of the week so Kailash team would be able to be up and running and get this thing going for you as early as Monday. I'll pause here. Any thoughts?

content.text:
Well, you know, we would just need Jim to on this part of the conversation because he'd be the ultimate approver for the costs and everything, so. I mean, to me, it looks comparable to what, you know, the other offer was.
So.

content.text:
Okay, right on. Thinking back to our conversation we had the other day... Spencer, and this is actually something you had touched on as well, too, which is to say, "Look at all things equal, apples to apples."
If the numbers are similar, we favor the idea of having it be an automated AI scalable solution versus option B, which is "I'm offshoring this to the Philippines. Like we wouldn't prefer this approach. Is that safe to say there.
And Spencer.

content.text: Yes, I agree with that.

So during this timeline, we would start out with the two weeks initial to understand each of these documents. What is the variance of these documents? What fields do we need to extract from this and what are the fields that need to get back into Salesforce or the Excel sheet?
So the initial two weeks would play a critical role that my team would work along with you guys to understand the current business process, how you guys are doing it and how the whole integration should work.
Then from the third week, they would start implementing and testing it. By the end of eight weeks, they would hand it over for you guys to test. Once you guys test it and approve that, "Hey, everything looks good." Then we will be going live.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: That sounds to make sense. I don't know if you have questions.

content.speaker: Speaker 4

content.speaker: kailash chanda

I think you know the guy better than anybody here. So what do you...? Where do you...? Is this something that you think is going to be appealing? Jim? Anything you think you might be wondering asking for us for Kailash that we get ahead of?

content.text:

content.text:

So we can understand, you know, how much it might take away from normal activities during production. And that might be something that would be good to understand. I don't know if that's been discussed.
And maybe I wasn't there for that.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: So heading. Spencer, as I mentioned, the first two weeks are the part that we would play. We would schedule 30 to 45-minute meetings for the first two weeks because that's where we understand what exactly the...

But after the eighth week, probably, let's say a week off time for you guys to test it, verify it. It depends how soon and how fast you guys can test and validate. But once you guys validate and then we are live.
So the majority of the time that we would ask is in the first two weeks. Rest all would be the more the first two weeks are efficient. The rest of the weeks are very minimal.

content.text: Okay. That makes...

content.speaker: Speaker 5

Spencer, and once you go live, that is to make sure that whatever solution the team has built is working fine and everything is in place.
So the team would be supporting you after the go-live for two weeks, and that is included as part of the scope, just to make sure that everything is fine. So once to the four weeks, two weeks we would need the access, but after that two weeks then Vijay's guys could remove the access.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: I just have one final question. Kailash, please don't get too far into the weeds on this, but are you going to be using MuleSoft or what's the middleware that you're going to be using to link all this stuff together?

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: So? Yes.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: Yes.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: That's right.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: Okay, I appreciate all that information. I'm good from my side, Ann, unless you've got something else.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Yeah, I think that was all good.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Okay.

content.speaker: Speaker 5
content.text: Okay, right on, Walton Spencer, appreciate the questions and appreciate the time and a little bit of the insight there for Jim. Speaking of Jim, I know he's traveling, I think he's still... Is he traveling Tomort still or is he back tomorrow? I can't remember.

content.text: They're flying back today and then he's at the Avis tomorrow, but we can still reach him. He'll be more reachable tomorrow. Let's do it that way.

content.speaker: Speaker 5
content.text: Okay? Yeah, and I think. What do you think? It would be a good time to reach up because I think that basically, I'm sure you guys will talk. Well, of course. Send this over and he'll, you know, being on the plane whenever he gets it and get some initial thoughts there. Would love to circle back, given we're thinking about... "Hey, let's start this thing on Monday. We'd love to just get his thoughts on this and see what we can do." Is there a time? Do you think that would be better for Jim that you'd be available tomorrow?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: I don't know. Because he is out of the office. I've had to reach out to him and see if he could give us a time that would work. I think...

content.speaker: Speaker 5
content.text:
That's fair. I know it's like a whole big act because it's like, "Well, I guess they'll be helping." So it's no longer the Pacific, the Central, or whatever. Why don't we just tentatively throw something for the same time tomorrow if that works?
Then, once you talk to him, if there's a better time that works there, we can adjust. What do we say about that as the next step and just get feedback then?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: I think that's fine.

content.speaker: Speaker 5
content.text: Okay, right on. Cool. Well, let's go ahead and do that, and Nicole, we'll go ahead and send out the invite, guys. Thank you again, Sage. Anything to add on your end before we call in here?

content.speaker: Speaker 6
content.text:
No, I just want to say thank you and Spencer for the time. Let us know if there are any questions. We're excited for this. I think we're talking to each other at the right time, and I think there are a lot of exciting possibilities ahead.
So I want to make sure we get started on the right foot. But excited to get this kicked off. Appreciate it.

content.speaker: Speaker 5
content.text: Yeah. Right on. Well, thank you guys so much. Pleasure talking as always, and we'll see you again tomorrow. Thanks, guys. Appreciate it. Appreciate it... By take care by guys.
